title: Hotfix a release while main has unreleased work

scenario.brief:
Production is on `release/1.0`. A bug there needs fixing now — but you **cannot** just ship `main`: it has an unfinished discounts feature that isn't ready for customers.

The pattern is: fix on the release line, ship it, then carry the same fix forward to `main` so it isn't lost in the next release.

**Steps.**

1. Branch from the release: `git switch -c hotfix/tax release/1.0`.
2. Fix `src/tax.js` (it should round the tax) and commit.
3. Put the fix on the release line: `git switch release/1.0` then `git merge hotfix/tax`.
4. Carry it to `main` without dragging the release's older state: `git switch main` then `git cherry-pick hotfix/tax`.

At the end, both `release/1.0` and `main` have the fix, and `main` still has its unreleased discounts work.
scenario.whyItMatters: Real products always have a released line and an ahead-of-release `main`. Hotfixing means fixing where customers are, then forward-porting — without shipping half-done work and without losing the fix at the next release. It's a core on-call skill.

files.src/invoice.js:
const { tax } = require('./tax')
module.exports = { grandTotal: (s) => s + tax(s) }

debrief.summary: You fixed a bug on the released line, shipped it there, and forward-ported the same fix to main — without releasing main's unfinished work and without losing the fix.
internals: Branching the hotfix from `release/1.0` meant the fix was built against what customers actually run, not against main's newer state.
Merging the hotfix into `release/1.0` fast-forwarded the release to include the fix, ready to ship as a patch.
Cherry-picking the hotfix commit onto `main` re-applied just that change, leaving main's unreleased discounts untouched.
Both lines now contain the fix; if you had only fixed the release, the next release from main would reintroduce the bug.

keyCommands.note: Branch the fix from the released line.
Land the fix on the release branch.
Forward-port the same fix onto main.

commonMistakes: Fixing on main and trying to ship main — which also ships unfinished work.
Fixing only the release and forgetting to forward-port, so the next release regresses.
Merging the whole release branch into main instead of cherry-picking the one fix.
debrief.atWork: This is the standard hotfix flow for any project with a maintained release. Fix where customers are, ship, then forward-port, so the fix survives into the future.
debrief.interview: "Production is broken but main has unreleased work — how do you ship a fix?" Answer: branch the fix from the release, merge and release it there, then cherry-pick it onto main.

solution: git commit -am "fix: round tax to whole cents"
